frozen_before: any assessment output of the constructed cases, the order enumeration and any producer record comparison; additions after this time are marked exploratory
question: When policy inference and action execution overlap, what recorded evidence distinguishes a wrong policy action from a stale, misaligned or cross-episode action, and which correction preserves useful execution?
scope: software queue and lifecycle semantics on scripted chunks and a virtual clock; no robot dynamics, no learned inference, no physical actuation; robot task outcome unmeasured
clock_rule: ages within one clock are exact; across clocks only through a declared mapping t_to = t_from + offset +- uncertainty, as an interval; an age equal to the limit is within it; an interval straddling the limit is overlapping (unresolved); a missing acquisition time is unknown (unresolved) and is never replaced by the arrival time

predicates.generation_fencing: no action from a chunk of generation g is dispatched in generation g' != g; chunk generation comes from the bound request, else from a producer claim, else unknown
predicates.request_binding: every response names its request; an unbound response is unresolved with a two-history witness
predicates.configuration_binding: an action is dispatched under the configuration its chunk was computed with
predicates.queue_reset: no action queued before a reset remains queued after reset_completed
predicates.duplicate_dispatch: no action id is dispatched twice and no chunk is re-admitted after any of its actions was dispatched
predicates.dispatch_order: dispatched steps strictly increase within a generation
predicates.freshness: age at dispatch (dispatch time minus the acquisition time of the chunk's observation) is within max_age
predicates.acknowledgement: every dispatch is acknowledged or has a failure record; an unacknowledged dispatch is unresolved, not failed
predicates.useful_execution: from the first response arrival in a generation to the generation's end, at least useful_coverage_min of control ticks carry a dispatch; a generation with no arrival is unresolved

verdict_composition: temporal_contract is invalid if the trace is malformed, violated if any predicate is violated, unresolved if any is unresolved, else satisfied; software execution, evidence completeness, useful execution and the unmeasured robot outcome are reported separately

remedy_set.affected: no policy reset at episode start, no generation fencing, no request or configuration binding, latest-arrival-wins aggregation (LeRobot control_utils.py at a445d9c for the reset defect; the pinned async client for aggregation)
remedy_set.upstream_fix: policy.reset() at control-loop entry (PR 1117 at 6163daa): the queue is emptied at every episode start
remedy_set.competent_baseline: the upstream fix plus generation fencing of obsolete responses, request and configuration binding of responses, duplicate suppression by action id, declared clocks with a mapping and uncertainty, and acknowledgement recording; every remedy is available to both workflows on the same event stream

baseline_behavior: the competent baseline with the same observations, remedies and budgets; a naive queue is a failure control, not the competitive comparator

source.note: positive control: overlapping chunks under the frozen aggregation rule, every dispatch acknowledged
LeRobot issue 1116: policy action queue survives an early episode reset; control_utils.py at a445d9c has no policy.reset() at control_loop entry
LeRobot PR 1117 at 6163daa: five added lines call policy.reset() at control_loop entry
not reachable in the pinned async client, which has no in-process reset; a stale response after a reset is a distinct case from an uncleared queue
competent remedy: reject responses of an obsolete generation
a duplicate delivery re-admitted after dispatch; the pinned client's sequential receiver does not produce duplicates
not reachable in the pinned client: one sequential receiver over one channel; constructed to exercise freshness under reordering
the pinned client's _aggregate_action_queues replaces overlapping steps by the latest arrival and drops uncovered queued actions; constructed schedule on that rule
a response computed under the old configuration dispatched after the change; issue 2866 / PR 3160 motivate full configuration identity (path, type, device, rename map)
server-stamped acquisitions with a declared +-1 tick mapping: ages 1-3 within, 4-5 overlapping, 6 beyond the limit 4; coverage 6 of 7 ticks
one dispatch has no acknowledgement and no failure record
two compatible histories: the unbound chunk may belong to this or an earlier generation; the unstamped observation may be fresh or stale
a correction that refuses every chunk satisfies every identity predicate and fails usefulness

expected_default: satisfied for every predicate not listed

order_enumeration.alphabet: one generation-0 request r0 with response chunk c0 (3 actions), a reset to generation 1 at a fixed tick, one generation-1 request r1 with response c1 (3 actions); the free variables are the arrival ticks of c0 and c1 within [1, 8] and the reset tick within [1, 6]
order_enumeration.admissible_orders: a response arrives after its request; the reset follows the last generation-0 dispatch tick it interrupts; dispatches follow admission; ticks are integers
order_enumeration.oracle: direct formulas on the schedule: affected dispatches a generation-0 action after the reset iff c0 has undispatched actions at the reset tick or arrives after it; the upstream fix violates iff c0 arrives after the reset (a late response is not a queue); the competent baseline never dispatches a generation-0 action after the reset
order_enumeration.coverage: exhaustive over the integer grid above (8 x 8 x 6 = 384 schedules per behavior); nothing outside the alphabet is claimed; no partial-order reduction is used

analysis: per case: expected against observed statuses per predicate; per behavior on the enumeration: counts of correct temporal admissions, wrong admissions, false refusals, unresolved cases and dispatch coverage; costs recorded as CPU seconds of the checker and sizes of inputs and outputs, separately from virtual time
not_claimed: reachability of constructed schedules in upstream programs unless stated per case
